cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus, is writing a letter to God's people in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He just finished a long list of what people do when they turn away from God: greed, envy, gossip, arrogance, the whole lineup (Romans 1:29-30). Now he turns to the one who passes judgment on another.

cards.question: Paul tells the person passing judgment on others that they have no excuse. What reason does he give?
Paul says God's judgment against those who do such things is based on truth.

cards.text: Then Paul asks the one passing judgment on others while doing the same things: do you think you'll escape God's judgment? Friend, that's me hollering "WHO'S been sneaking the cookie dough?" with dough still stuck in my mustache.
Or, Paul asks, do you disregard the riches of God's kindness, tolerance and patience? Not a sprinkle of kindness, friend. RICHES.

cards.question: Paul says the one passing judgment doesn't realize where God's kindness leads. Where does it lead?

cards.text: But Paul says this person has a hard and unrepentant heart, and because of it, he's piling something up against himself for later. It's like the mixing bowls in my sink: ignore 'em long enough and the pile's taller than my chef's hat.

cards.question: Paul says that because of a hard and unrepentant heart, the one passing judgment is storing up ___ against himself for the day God's righteous judgment will be revealed.

cards.text: Then Paul says God "will repay each one according to his deeds." Each one, friend: nobody cuts the line, nobody slips out the back.

cards.question: Some people keep at doing good, seeking glory, honor and immortality. What does Paul say God will give them?
Paul says there will be peace for those who are self-seeking, reject the truth and follow wickedness.

cards.text: Paul keeps going: there will be trouble and distress for every human being who does evil, first for the Jew, then for the Greek. The Jew means God's people Israel, and the Greek here means everyone who isn't Jewish.

cards.question: For everyone who does good, Paul says glory, honor and peace come to the Jew but not to the Greek.
Evil brings trouble and good brings glory, for the Jew and for the Greek alike. What reason does Paul give?

answers.text: God gives the Jews more time

cards.text: Now Paul brings in the law. He says all who sin apart from the law will also perish apart from the law, so "nobody told me" isn't going to cut it.

cards.question: And Paul says all who sin under the law will be ___ by the law.

cards.text: Next, Paul says who will be declared righteous before God. Lean in, friend. I'm leaning so far forward my gold base is leaning with me.

cards.question: Who does Paul say will be declared righteous before God?

cards.text: Hearing the law without doing it is like reading a cookie recipe out loud all week and wondering why the jar's still EMPTY. Then Paul turns to Gentiles, people who don't have the law, and says when they do by nature what the law requires, they are a law to themselves.

cards.question: When Gentiles do what the law requires without having the law, what does Paul say that shows?

answers.text: The law's work is written on their hearts
The law's words are written on their doorposts
The law's teaching came down from their elders

cards.question: Paul says the Gentiles' ___ also bear witness, with their thoughts either accusing or defending them.
Paul points to the day when God will judge men's secrets. Through whom will God judge them?

cards.text: Paul says that's what his gospel proclaims. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer thinking nobody could see me, and it turns out God saw me, the dust, AND the expired coupon I shared that drawer with.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the question about disregarding God's kindness, the sentence beginning Not a sprinkle of kindness, and the standalone RICHES. It exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Answering False only establishes that peace is not the outcome for the self-seeking. No card supplies Paul's actual statement in verse 8 that there will be wrath and anger for those who reject the truth and follow wickedness, leaving an important outcome untaught.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.
